Phoenix to Tucson shuttle, private and chauffeured

Scottsdale Sprinters drives groups from Phoenix, Scottsdale and Sky Harbor to Tucson in a private chauffeured vehicle, door to door, and back again: for a drive of 2 hours each way, one way is $600 before 8% tax in the Luxury SUV (Suburban) for up to 6, or $730 in an Executive Sprinter for up to 14. You book the whole vehicle, not a seat. Below: the distance, the price for every vehicle, the ride back, and what is included. Questions? Call (623) 986-6339 or email reservations@scottsdalesprinters.com.

Last updated: September 27, 2026

How do you get from Phoenix to Tucson without driving?

Book a private chauffeured transfer: one vehicle for your group only, door to door from any Phoenix or Scottsdale address, Sky Harbor included, to your address in Tucson, with no shared stops and no timetable. In the Luxury SUV (Suburban), for up to 6 with 10 bags, if checkout measures the drive at 2 hours each way, one way is $600 before 8% tax. This is not a shared shuttle. A shared van sells seats on its own schedule; a private transfer leaves when you choose, from where you are, and goes where you are staying. The whole vehicle is yours, so the price does not change with the headcount. People book the run for a University of Arizona game or graduation, the gem shows, a Tucson resort, a flight out of Tucson International, or the ride home to Sky Harbor. Every figure on this page comes from the same rate grid and pricing engine as checkout.

How far is Tucson from Phoenix?

From Old Town Scottsdale: about 115 miles by road to downtown Tucson, about 1¾ to 2¼ hours each way without stops or traffic delays. From Phoenix Sky Harbor: about 110 miles by road to downtown Tucson, about 1¾ to 2 hours each way without stops or traffic delays. Your chauffeur plans the route; the checkout measures your own two addresses and prices from that drive.

How much is a private shuttle from Phoenix to Tucson?

It is priced from the drive, per vehicle, not per seat. If checkout measures the drive at 2 hours each way, one way before tax is $600 in the Luxury SUV (Suburban), $730 in the Executive Black Sprinter and $1,225 in the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax); both ways booked together is $1,080, $1,314 and $2,205. A transfer is flat within 15 road miles from pickup to drop-off, and priced from the drive beyond that, with the empty return included. Tucson is beyond it, so each vehicle's published transfer basis covers the first 60 minutes of vehicle time, out and empty back, and the rest of the drive is added by the half hour at the vehicle's hourly rate: $125 an hour in the Luxury SUV (Suburban), $145 in an Executive Sprinter. There is no hourly minimum on a transfer. The drive in these examples is a round figure inside the measured range. Checkout measures your own two addresses when you enter them and shows the exact total before you pay; a longer measured drive adds half hours, a shorter one removes them. Can you pick us up in Tucson for the ride back?

Yes. We collect in Tucson, at a home, a hotel, the university or Tucson International Airport (TUS), for the ride back to Phoenix, Scottsdale or Sky Harbor. Every trip on this page starts or ends in the Valley, and the ride back is priced the same way, from the measured drive. A Tucson pickup is confirmed in writing before you pay, with the address and the time. If you book the ride out and the ride back together, the return comes off 20%.

What is on the way to Tucson?

The route is Interstate 10 south the whole way. Picacho Peak State Park sits beside it at exit 219, the one landmark on the drive and a natural stretch stop. A stop on a transfer is $50; on an hourly day the stops are already yours. Downtown Tucson and Oro Valley have their own area guides below, with the addresses groups ask for most.

Can you meet us at Tucson International Airport?

Yes. Tucson International Airport (TUS) is on the south side of the city, and it lists chauffeured cars among its ground transportation. Give us the flight when you book; the pickup point is confirmed in writing. Flying into Sky Harbor and staying in Tucson is the more common shape: the chauffeur tracks the flight at Sky Harbor and drives you south.

Which vehicle should we book?

Pick by the group and the bags: the Luxury SUV (Suburban) seats 6 with room for 10 bags; an Executive Sprinter, black or white, seats 14 with room for 40; the Maybach Jet Sprinter seats 9 with room for 4 checked bags; the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) seats 29 with room for 30; the 56-Passenger Motorcoach seats 56 with room for 125. For two to four travellers with suitcases the Luxury SUV (Suburban) is the lowest total here, $600 one way at a 2 hours drive. A family or a team with golf bags or ski gear fits an Executive Sprinter. The Maybach Jet Sprinter is the most luxurious ride in the fleet, for a small group that wants massage seats and a table for the drive. A wedding party or a company offsite rides a coach.

One way, both ways, or a day trip?

One way is a transfer; there and back on different days is two transfers booked together; there and back the same day, with the vehicle waiting while you are in Tucson, is an hourly day. 8 hours in an Executive Sprinter is $1,015 before tax and $875 in the Luxury SUV (Suburban). Long days cost less per hour: book 7 hours or more and free hours come off at checkout automatically, so 8 hours bills 7. On an hourly day the stops are yours and the miles are not counted. The reservations desk confirms in writing which shape fits your day before you pay.

What is included, and what is added?

The chauffeur, the fuel and bottled water are in the price. Arizona sales tax of 8% is added at checkout, and gratuity is optional and never added for you. There is no booking fee and no fuel surcharge. On a transfer each added stop on the way is $50; a stretch stop you ask for is simply a stop. A 50% deposit holds the date and the balance is charged 48 hours before pickup. Passengers 21 and over may bring their own drinks on a for-hire vehicle in Arizona; the chauffeur never drinks, and if anyone under 21 rides, no alcohol comes on the trip. There is no smoking or vaping inside any vehicle.

Frequently asked questions

How much is a shuttle from Phoenix to Tucson?

A private transfer is priced from the drive: at 2 hours each way it is $600 one way before tax in the Luxury SUV (Suburban) for up to 6, and $730 in an Executive Sprinter for up to 14. Checkout measures your addresses and shows the exact total before you pay.

How far is Tucson from Phoenix?

From Old Town Scottsdale: about 115 miles by road to downtown Tucson, about 1¾ to 2¼ hours each way without stops or traffic delays. From Phoenix Sky Harbor: about 110 miles by road to downtown Tucson, about 1¾ to 2 hours each way without stops or traffic delays.

Is this a shared shuttle?

No. The vehicle is booked for your group only, door to door, on your schedule. You pay per vehicle, so a full cabin splits the same total.

Do you pick up at Sky Harbor for Tucson?

Yes. Give us the airline and flight number when you book and we track the flight; your chauffeur sends the pickup instruction for your terminal.

Is there a shuttle from Tucson to Phoenix Sky Harbor?

Yes, private: we collect at your Tucson address and drive you to your terminal at Sky Harbor. It is priced from the measured drive, like the ride south, and confirmed in writing before you pay.

How far in advance should we book?

Availability varies by date and by vehicle. Same-day bookings are welcome with no cutoff, subject to availability. Request a current quote for your date and we confirm in writing what is open.

Who drives, and is the company insured?

A professional chauffeur who is background and MVR checked and drug screened, and the company is licensed and insured with commercial coverage on every vehicle. Guests give us a 5.0-star Google rating across 511 reviews.
